summary: The sitting senator ran again. John Hickenlooper (Democrat) won a second term over Mark Baisley (Republican), a state senator, and several minor-party candidates.

candidates.name: John Hickenlooper
candidates.bio: Democratic U.S. senator from Colorado who trained as a geologist and, after being laid off, opened Colorado's first brewpub in Denver. He was elected mayor of Denver and later served as governor of Colorado, and is running for a second Senate term. He said in 2024 that this would be his last Senate campaign.

positions.summary: Says that as governor he moved Colorado from 40th in job creation to the number one economy.
Says he will work to lower health care and prescription drug costs, and cites expanding Medicaid to nearly 400,000 Coloradans as governor.
Says that as Denver mayor he worked to improve educational opportunities for Denver students.
Says he will protect public lands while fighting climate change, and cites what he calls pioneering anti-pollution climate measures as governor.
Said in May 2022, after the Senate blocked the Women's Health Protection Act, that Republicans "voted today to put politics between women and their doctors."

candidates.name: Mark Baisley
candidates.bio: Republican state senator for Colorado's 4th district since 2023 and a state representative from 2019 to 2023. He is an aerospace engineer by background and president of a software company, and entered the U.S. Senate race in January 2026 after suspending his campaign for governor. He was born in 1955 in Hastings, Minnesota, and earned a degree from Columbia College in Missouri.

positions.summary: Says he will fight to cut federal taxes, roll back job-killing regulations and restore American energy dominance.
Writes that about 1.2 million people are legally invited to live in the United States each year and that applicants are vetted to make sure they will assimilate into American culture.
Said in March 2026 that schools should "train kids for real jobs, not woke lectures."
Co-sponsored a 2025 special-session bill that would end Colorado's OmniSalud program by blocking undocumented residents from insurance paid for by the state's affordability enterprise.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (political.org Nov 14 tally, AP called 34 of 35)
